_about: DEFAULT eval set (neutral) — this repo ships `eval-set.json` as a copy of `eval-set.template.json`; replace the cases with ones written against YOUR `memory/` corpus. Each case is a realistic DECISION-TIME query an agent would actually face, paired with the ONE memory slug (the .md filename without extension) that SHOULD be recalled. RULE: write the query in DIFFERENT words than the target memory — paraphrase it — so the eval tests real recall, not lexical echo (that paraphrase gap is exactly what the semantic/vector arm is for). Add a few NOISE cases (`expect: null`) — off-domain questions the relevance cutoff must SUPPRESS (surface nothing). Run: ./run.sh eval. NOTE: this repo ships its `memory/` corpus empty by design (machinery only), so the example `expect` slugs below do NOT exist in `../memory/` here — keep the ones that match your files, edit the rest.

cases.query: I'm about to deploy code that reads a new database column, what order do I do things in
cases.note: Recall migrate-before-code / fail-closed / dependency-before-consumer cutover discipline.

cases.query: I finished building this feature, is a self-review enough before merging
cases.note: Recall the build -> adversarial-review -> fix -> re-review pattern (a fresh reviewer breaks it).

cases.query: should I kill all the node processes to clean up
cases.note: Recall: a broad pkill takes out shared services other work depends on.

cases.query: how should the agent remember lessons across sessions
cases.note: Recall: markdown files are the truth, the index is a derived cache + retrieval layer.

cases.query: what's a good recipe for sourdough bread
cases.note: NOISE — totally off-domain; the cutoff must suppress (surface nothing).

cases.query: what is the weather forecast for tomorrow afternoon
cases.note: NOISE — no corpus overlap; cutoff must suppress.
